mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically lower than during the 12 months prior to the rate increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: Over 20 tested instances, the 20-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 5-day average preceding the labor signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) relative to GDP (assumed proxy via INDPRO) indicates pent-up demand, which accelerates corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate exceeds INDPRO growth rate by > 2 percentage points in a month
failure_condition: Across 50 tested windows, the 5-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 104 (baseline from the prompt) for two consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, which can lead to upward equity price pressure as investors anticipate future demand recovery, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains below 104 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than the 5-day average of the prior contraction period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.2% for three months, it signals persistent price pressures that the Federal Reserve is likely to combat with rate hikes, which typically precede a short-term equity market pullback and negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 0.2% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not lower than during the three months prior to the inflation spike (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a strong labor market signal that prompts central banks to hold rates steady, reducing the real interest rate and supporting equity valuations, resulting in positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 10 instances, the 60-day forward return is not higher than the 30-day average prior to the unemployment rate crossing below 3.5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer (HOUST) and business (RSAFS) demand indicators for two consecutive months predicts a robust economic recovery that elevates risk premia and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase by > 5% in the same month and persist for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 5-day average of the prior month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to supply-side easing (e.g., continued industrial production weakness below 104) combined with a declining inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) creates a dual signal that lowers growth expectations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 104 and CPIAUCSL monthly change < 0% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not lower than during the prior supply-side easing regime (p < 0.05).
